title: Two numbers that add up
prompt:
Write two_sum(numbers, target) that returns a list [i, j] of two different positions (i < j) whose numbers add up to target, or None if there is no such pair.
In the tests there is never more than one right answer.
hints: Pick one number. What other number would you need to reach the target? How could you find out whether it exists in the list?
Looping over every pair works, but a dictionary that remembers the numbers you've already passed lets you look up 'the missing partner' directly.

Plan: go through the list with positions; for each number compute its partner (target minus number); if the partner was seen before return both positions; otherwise remember this number and its position. Return None at the end.

edge_hints.duplicates: The same VALUE can appear twice, at different positions. Make sure you don't use the same position twice, but do allow equal values.
edge_hints.none: If no pair exists you must return None after checking everything.
edge_hints.zero: Zero is a normal number; don't treat 0 as 'missing' (watch out for `if position:` checks).
edge_hints.empty: An empty list has no pair; return None.
edge_hints.single: One number can't pair with itself.
